skill.name: doc-generator
skill.description: Generate structured Markdown documentation for Python files and packages from docstrings, type hints, classes, functions, and code structure.
skill.summary: Turn Python source files into organized Markdown API references and README content.
skill.author: bossjones

security_audit.summary: All eight static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences or inline code formatting in SKILL.md. The skill contains no shell commands, prompt injection, network instructions, or semantic evidence of malicious intent.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks at line 29 open a Markdown example block; no command or executable Ruby expression appears in the cited range.
Line 41 uses inline Markdown backticks to format a method signature, not to invoke a shell command.
Line 50 uses inline Markdown backticks around a parameter name, with no executable content.
Line 57 declares a fenced Python example in Markdown and does not execute Python, Ruby, or shell code.
Line 59 closes the fenced Python example; the backticks are Markdown delimiters rather than command execution syntax.
Line 60 closes the outer Markdown example block and contains no command or dynamic expression.
Line 85 formats the Python standard-library module name ast with inline Markdown backticks; it does not execute a command.
Line 86 formats the Python standard-library module name inspect with inline Markdown backticks; it does not execute a command.

content.value_statement: Python documentation often becomes incomplete or inconsistent when maintained manually. This skill converts source structure, docstrings, and type hints into organized Markdown.
actual_capabilities: Processes one Python file, a recursive directory, or a specified file list.
Extracts module, class, function, and method documentation with available type hints.
Organizes generated Markdown by modules, classes, methods, and functions.
Handles Google, NumPy, and Sphinx docstring formats.
Reports syntax errors and missing documentation while continuing with valid files.
limitations: The workflow is designed for Python source code only.
Documentation quality depends on available docstrings, names, and type hints.
Private members are excluded unless the user requests them.
The skill produces Markdown, not a hosted documentation website.

use_cases.title: Document a New Python Module
use_cases.description: Create a clear API reference from a module before sharing it with a team.

use_cases.title: Build Package Documentation
use_cases.description: Generate consistent Markdown pages across a Python package for onboarding and maintenance.

use_cases.title: Refresh a Project README
use_cases.description: Summarize public classes, functions, signatures, and usage details from the current source.

prompt_templates.title: Document One File
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate Markdown documentation for [file_path], including its module summary, public classes, functions, parameters, returns, and available examples.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create basic documentation for a single Python file.

prompt_templates.title: Document a Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Recursively document Python files in [directory_path] and organize the result by module, class, method, and function.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a structured reference for a Python package.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Focused README
prompt_templates.prompt: Create README content from [directory_path], emphasizing installation context, public APIs, type hints, and concise usage examples.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare project documentation for repository visitors.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Generate Advanced Docs
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [file_list], include requested private members, preserve supported docstring formatting, add navigation, and identify missing documentation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Produce detailed documentation while identifying source documentation gaps.

output_examples.output: A Markdown reference with the module overview, public classes, method signatures, parameters, returns, and usage guidance.

output_examples.input: Generate API documentation for the src/services directory.
output_examples.output: A hierarchical Markdown document organized by service module, class, method, and function, with a table of contents.

output_examples.input: Create README documentation and note missing docstrings.
output_examples.output: README-ready sections describing public interfaces, followed by clear notices for undocumented classes and functions.

best_practices: Provide exact file or directory paths and state whether private members should be included.
Review source docstrings and type hints before generation for more complete output.
Specify the intended audience and desired Markdown structure.
anti_patterns: Do not expect accurate descriptions when source names and docstrings provide no context.
Do not use the skill for non-Python languages.
Do not publish generated documentation without reviewing signatures, examples, and missing descriptions.

faq.question: Can it document an entire Python package?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a directory path, and the workflow recursively processes Python files.

faq.question: Which docstring formats are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow supports Google, NumPy, and Sphinx docstring structures.

faq.question: Does it include private members?
faq.answer: Private members are skipped by default and can be included when explicitly requested.

faq.question: What happens when a file has syntax errors?
faq.answer: The workflow reports the error, skips that file, and continues processing valid files.

faq.question: Does it require external dependencies?
faq.answer: No external dependency is required for the basic documentation workflow.

faq.question: Can it create a hosted documentation site?
faq.answer: No. It generates Markdown content that can be added to a repository or documentation platform.
